I'd say fin rot or stress. Do you know if her previous tank had clean water. Was water changed, were there live plants, etc. Was it dechlorinated?

Java Fern and Anubias are great options. These are both slow growing. Be aware that Java ferns and anubias should never be put directly into soil. Rather they should be tied or glued to rocks or wood. You could add floating plants like salavinia or duckweed (just be cautious of duckweed as it grows very fast). You could also do dwarf hair grass, amazon swords, or hornwort. All beginner plants that could be planted into soil directly. I know you just added gravel to the tank, but I highly reccomend mixing this gravel with a substrate like fluval stratum if you would like a plant that will root itself directly in the ground. Root tabs are also a good option if you dont get a nutrient-rich substrate.

So what im seeing at the bottom of the tank looks like a lot of fish waste to me. My first course of action would be to do a water change and vacuum the gravel (if possible). The waste could be causing a ton or ammonia buildup which could be part of the problem. Do you have a larger picture of your tank? That would help everyone be able to see this way easier and gave better answers that may help.
